checks.why: a @PreAuthorize expression that calls @bean.method(...) links the guarded method to the bean's method, as a framework hop and not a call
the guard's impact names every method its expression guards, @PostFilter included, labelled framework-mediated
the bean name is resolved as the container names it (a decapitalized class name), and the overload is chosen by the number of arguments written
near miss: the one-argument overload guards the method whose expression passes one argument, not the one passing two
and the two-argument overload guards only the method passing two
near miss: a bean reference with a name no bean has links nothing, though a class of that simple name declares the method
near miss: the guard's name inside a role string is not a bean reference
a bean's own override is the method the expression runs: it is linked, and the interface method it implements is not linked a second time
near miss: the interface method the bean overrides gets no framework row of its own
